events.title: robots.txt becomes an IETF standard (RFC 9309) - and says it is not access control
events.place: IETF Administration LLC (publisher of the RFC series), Wilmington, Delaware
events.summary: The Robots Exclusion Protocol - the robots.txt convention that crawlers had followed informally since the early web - was published as Standards Track RFC 9309 in September 2022, authored by Martijn Koster and three Google engineers. events.title: IETF charters the AI Preferences (AIPREF) working group
events.place: IETF Administration LLC, Wilmington, Delaware
events.summary: The IETF approved the charter of the AI Preferences working group to standardise a vocabulary for expressing how content may be used for AI training and use, and ways to attach those preferences through robots.txt and HTTP headers. events.title: EU 'Digital Omnibus' proposes that websites must honour automated, machine-readable privacy choices
events.place: European Commission, Berlaymont building, Brussels
events.summary: The Commission's Digital Omnibus proposal, COM(2025) 837, would insert Article 88b into the GDPR: controllers' online interfaces must let people give or refuse consent and object 'through automated and machine-readable means', controllers must respect those choices, European standards bodies would draft the interpretation standards, and large browser providers would have to support the signals 48 months after entry into force. A proposed Article 88c would let AI development rely on legitimate interests subject to an 'unconditional right to object'. On 10 February 2026 the EDPB and EDPS 'strongly welcome[d]' Article 88b.
events.significance: For the first time an EU legislative text would oblige organisations to accept a person's own machine-readable signal as the expression of their choice - the regulatory opening an IEEE 7012 agent needs.

events.title: IEEE publishes 7012-2025 ('MyTerms'): personal privacy terms that people's agents proffer
events.place: IEEE Standards Association, 445 Hoes Lane, Piscataway, New Jersey

Individuals act as first parties and point to standard-form terms from a roster kept by a neutral non-business body; if the second party agrees, both sides or their agents sign and each keeps a matching record that can be retrieved, audited or disputed. The project's PAR had been approved on 6 December 2017.
events.significance: It is the first standard in which the person, through their own agent, offers the terms and the organisation accepts them, with records on both sides - the inversion of the click-through model that delegated AI agents otherwise inherit.

events.place: Council of the European Union, Europa building, Brussels

myths.claim: IEEE 7012 / MyTerms is just another browser flag like Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control.
myths.correction: DNT and GPC are one-way signals responding to choices framed by sites. IEEE 7012 makes the individual the first party who proffers standard-form contractual terms; the site accepts one, both sides (or their agents) sign, and each keeps a matching record that can be audited or disputed. The transport may resemble a browser header, but the legal form - an agreement with records - is different. (The characterisation of MyTerms as enforceable contract is the project's own and is untested in court.)

agentScenario.supportInPublicMaterials: IEEE 7012 abstract: records must be retrievable, auditable or disputable. How a breach is detected, and which forum hears the dispute, is not specified in public materials.

sources.title: IEEE 7012-2025 (standard page)
sources.quote: a matching record shall be kept by both sides in a form that can be retrieved, audited, or disputed, if necessary, at some later time--and which is available to do so easily.
